story: story-009 (stateless looper) hardened by story-014 (pin dispatcherIndex + derive paymentToken), story-015 (minReward slippage floor), story-016 (snapshot nudge pot before mint loop)

verifiedProperties.noUnboundedLoopsNote: batchMint loops `count` times over a caller-supplied `count` with no upper bound; self-bounded economically (each iteration is a real paid mint at the dispatcher's ramping price) and by block gas — only the caller is harmed, no third-party DoS.
verifiedProperties.checkedArithmeticNote: Solidity 0.8.20; no `unchecked` blocks, no assembly. Only arithmetic is the loop counter, `remaining / DUST_THRESHOLD`, and `paymentAmount - remaining` (guarded by ternary).
verifiedProperties.reentrancyGuardedNote: batchMint has NO ReentrancyGuard. Safe only under the no-callback-token trust assumption (see trustAssumptions). Exploitability deferred to interaction analysis.
verifiedProperties.accessControlNote: All admin setters are onlyOwner; pause/unpause are onlyPauser. batchMint is permissionless (whenNotPaused only).
verifiedProperties.initializerProtectedNote: Not upgradeable; configured via constructor `Ownable(initialOwner)` + owner setters.
verifiedProperties.pausableNote: Hybrid OZ Pausable + IPausable; only batchMint is whenNotPaused. Admin setters and rescueERC20 stay callable while paused.

localFindings.description: `for (uint256 i; i < count; ++i) nftMinter.mint(...)` iterates over caller-controlled `count` with no cap. Each iteration is a genuine paid mint (the minter pulls the dispatcher's ramping price from this contract per call), so the loop is self-bounded by the caller's own gas and payment budget. There is no shared/queue state, so a large `count` only reverts the caller's own tx (out-of-gas or insufficient paymentAmount); no third party is griefed.
localFindings.recommendation: No fix required for safety. Optionally document a practical max-count for the frontend. Informational only.
localFindings.deferNote: Not a DoS on other users — flagged for completeness per the local-loop checklist.

localFindings.description: batchMint makes multiple external calls (paymentToken.safeTransferFrom from msg.sender; configs()/primeToken() reads; the mint loop into the trusted minter -> dispatcher, which donates the nudge token in during the loop; nudge safeTransfer to caller-controlled `recipient`; payment refund safeTransfer to msg.sender) while the contract custodies a nudge pot — yet carries no nonReentrant guard. With the owner-configured payment/nudge tokens being callback-free standard ERC20s (USDC / dispatcher prime token / phUSD), there is no reentrancy entrypoint. A token with a transfer/receive hook (ERC777-style) on either the payment or nudge token would open a reentry path that could re-enter batchMint mid-loop and re-snapshot/re-pay the pot.
localFindings.recommendation: Either add OZ ReentrancyGuard to batchMint as defence-in-depth, or keep the explicit invariant that nudgePaymentToken and the dispatcher prime token must be callback-free standard ERC20s. Exploitability depends on the concrete configured tokens — deferred to interaction analysis.
localFindings.deferNote: Reentrancy exploitability requires knowing the configured token implementations; surfaced as a trust assumption, not asserted as exploitable.

externalEntryPoints.function: batchMint(uint256 count, address recipient, uint256 paymentAmount, uint256 minReward) returns (uint256 totalPaid)
stateChanges: transient allowance to tokenMinter (set max, revoked to 0 within the call)
valueFlows: PAY mints: tokenMinter.mint() x count pulls dispatcher price from this via the max approval
INFLOW during loop: dispatcher donates nudgePaymentToken into this on each mint (the 'donate-forward' pot funding)
PAYOUT nudge: nudgeAmount (PRE-loop snapshot) -> recipient, if count>=nudgeSize and feature active
REFUND: residual paymentToken -> msg.sender iff residual >= DUST_THRESHOLD (1e6 wei)
reverts: inner mint revert if paymentAmount under-funds cumulative dispatcher cost (atomic rollback)
externalEntryPoints.returns: totalPaid = paymentAmount - refundedSurplus (or paymentAmount if residual sub-threshold)

externalEntryPoints.notes: 0 disables batchMint (sentinel; V2 nextIndex starts at 1). Callable while paused.
address(0) disables pausing. Callable while paused.

externalEntryPoints.function: rescueERC20(IERC20 token, address to, uint256 amount)
externalEntryPoints.notes: Owner escape hatch; can also drain the nudge pot. Owner-trusted. Callable while paused. Explicit `amount` so it composes with the pot rather than full-sweep.

externalCalls.target: ITokenMinterV2 tokenMinter (owner-set; cast to INFTMinterV2 for configs())
externalCalls.trustLevel: trusted (owner-configured, OUT OF SCOPE sibling NFTMinterV2)
externalCalls.notes: Pinning the minter to owner state (story-014) is the fix for prior H-01: a caller-supplied no-op minter could clear the count>=nudgeSize gate and drain the pot without paying. Now mints genuinely charge the dispatcher's ramping price.

paymentToken is DERIVED from dispatcher.primeToken() (story-014), not caller-supplied — eliminates wrong/zero payment-asset attacks. Also the off-chain actor that donates nudgePaymentToken into this contract per mint (pot funding).

Assumes no transfer hook and no fee-on-transfer; a fee-on-transfer prime token would under-fund mints and/or skew the dust sweep. Per repo known-invalid list, weird/FoT tokens are out of scope unless USDT.
MUST differ from paymentToken whenever configured (enforced up-front). Funded externally (yield funnel). Snapshot taken BEFORE the mint loop (story-016).
Receives an ERC20 transfer only (no callback for standard tokens) plus the ERC1155 mints routed by the minter. No value-control beyond being the payout/mint sink chosen by the caller.

stateVariables.name: DUST_THRESHOLD
stateVariables.note: residual below this is kept (JS rounding slack)

nudgePotMechanism.summary: Owner-administered incentive: when count>=nudgeSize and nudgePaymentToken is set, the contract pays the snapshotted nudge-token balance to recipient after the mint loop, before the dust refund.
nudgePotMechanism.funding: Externally funded (yield funnel directing e.g. USDC into this contract) AND per-mint: the dispatcher donates the nudge token into this contract on every mint during the loop (the 'donate-forward' mechanic).
nudgePotMechanism.snapshot: story-016: nudgeAmount = balanceOf(nudgePaymentToken) is read BEFORE the payment pull and mint loop (line 271-275). So a qualifying batcher is paid only the PRIOR accumulated pot; its own loop's per-mint donations accrue AFTER the snapshot and remain in the contract to seed the NEXT claimant.
nudgePotMechanism.consumption: After the loop and allowance-revoke (line 294-297): IERC20(nudgePaymentToken).safeTransfer(recipient, nudgeAmount); emit NudgePaid. nudgeAmount==0 path is a no-op.
nudgePotMechanism.slippageFloor: story-015: if nudgeAmount < minReward, revert BatchMint__RewardBelowMinimum -> rolls back mints + payment pull (line 290-292). minReward==0 disables the floor.

priorFindings.H-01: value-blind nudge drain via caller-supplied no-op minter clearing the numeric count>=nudgeSize gate. FIXED by story-014 (minter pinned to owner state; paymentToken derived from dispatcher prime token; faked/mismatched token reverts the real mint and rolls back).
priorFindings.M-01_MEV: front-run of the balance-based payout — whoever qualifies first takes the entire pot. ACKNOWLEDGED. story-015's minReward only stops the loser from minting for a sub-floor reward; it does NOT stop the front-runner from winning the pot.

localInvariantCandidates: NUDGE-SNAPSHOT-SOLVENCY: at the nudge safeTransfer (line 295), balanceOf(nudgePaymentToken) >= nudgeAmount always holds, because between the pre-loop snapshot and the transfer the nudge balance only increases (per-mint donations) and the payment pull cannot touch it (nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken is enforced). => the nudge transfer can never revert for insufficient balance and never over-pays the prior pot.
NUDGE-PAYOUT-BOUND: nudgeAmount paid out <= nudge-token balance held at function entry (the PRIOR pot); this batch's own per-mint donations are never refunded to the current caller.
NUDGE-GATE: nudgeAmount > 0 only when (nudgeSize != 0 && count >= nudgeSize && nudgePaymentToken != 0 && pre-loop balance > 0).
MIN-REWARD-FLOOR: any successful batchMint with minReward>0 delivered nudgeAmount >= minReward to recipient.

ALLOWANCE-HYGIENE: the minter allowance is set to type(uint256).max at line 278 and reset to 0 at line 284 within the same call => no residual allowance persists across batchMint calls (forceApprove handles non-zero->non-zero tokens).
PAYMENT-TOKEN-DERIVATION: paymentToken is always == ITokenDispatcherV2(configs(dispatcherIndex).dispatcher).primeToken(); never caller-supplied.
NUDGE-DISTINCTNESS: whenever nudgePaymentToken != 0, batchMint only proceeds when nudgePaymentToken != paymentToken (else reverts before any funds move).
DUST-RETENTION: residual paymentToken < DUST_THRESHOLD (1e6) is retained; residual >= DUST_THRESHOLD is fully swept to msg.sender (including any third-party donation, by acknowledged design).
TOTALPAID-CONSISTENCY: totalPaid == paymentAmount - refunded (refunded = residual when swept, else 0), clamped at 0 when residual > paymentAmount (donation case).
trustAssumptions: tokenMinter is the owner-configured, trusted NFTMinterV2 implementing both ITokenMinterV2.mint and INFTMinterV2.configs; a minter not implementing configs reverts batchMint.
The pinned dispatcher's primeToken() returns a callback-free, non-fee-on-transfer standard ERC20 (e.g. USDC/phUSD).
nudgePaymentToken is a callback-free standard ERC20 distinct from the prime token.

The dispatcher donates the nudge token into this contract on each mint (the assumption that funds the donate-forward pot); the contract does not enforce this — if no donation occurs the pot only grows from external funding.

Owner is non-malicious (Law 3): rescueERC20 can drain the pot and owner can disable the feature; not treated as an attack. Setting nudgePaymentToken == prime token is an obvious, loud, up-front revert (config-time), not a hidden footgun.
pauser address is trusted to pause/unpause batchMint.
